# EN 301 549 adoption research

Follow [workflow](../workflow.md), [evidence](../evidence.md), [review](../review.md) and [shared storage](../research/README.md). This specification applies only to `EN 301 549 adoptation.md` in the testing repository. The user authorised setup, baseline research and recurring maintenance on 27 September 2026. Never approve, merge, enable auto-merge or write main. Only the user can explicitly change the no-merge rule; continuing work or passing checks cannot change it.

## Scope and records

The initial scope is the 14 existing rows. Keep the filename for inbound links. Country evidence belongs in `research/countries/<country>.json`, `domains.adoption`, sharing that country's evidence pool. Extend `registry.json` for adoption-only countries without inventing other domains. The European standard and EU-wide citation history belong in `adoption/european-standard.json`, with `subject`, `evidence` and `adoption` keys; the EU is not a new country. The page registry in evidence.md owns the destination. `check_adoption.py` validates both storage locations. Do not create parallel writable country records.

Each domain contains claims, questions, attempts, review dates, a public-row mapping and a review-report path. `public_cells` maps all five cell indices to claim IDs. The frozen inherited-row snapshot is pinned by digest: any changed factual cell requires verified evidence and isolated review, even if the claim has inherited provenance. Empty mappings cannot exempt changed wording. Only the Europe/European Union label and an unchanged empty-link destination labelled “Source document (PDF)” are editorial exceptions. Split inherited assertions into status, date, edition and extra claims; preserve exact inherited text and provenance. A claim's `existing_text` is null for new assertions. Stable claim IDs survive edits; changed evidence creates a new fingerprint in the shared pool. Retain old sources and supersession history in review notes rather than overwriting history. No country-wide verified flag exists.

## Evidence checklist

For each row establish issuer, national identifier, exact EN edition, relationship (identical adoption, modified adoption, reference, or unknown), draft/final/withdrawn stage, and scope. Research standards adoption independently of legal use, procurement requirements and voluntary guidance. A standards body's own catalogue can establish publication/adoption; legislation or official gazettes establish legal effect. An industry report cannot establish nationwide law. Record applicable sectors/audiences, amendments and supersession separately. Never update every country's edition when ETSI publishes a revision.

Every claim records `aspect`, `statement`, `scope`, `stage`, `status`, `source_refs`, `event_dates`, `attempted_on`, `verified_on`, `next_review_due`, `existing_text` and `review_note`. Each date has a `kind` and `value`; a projected milestone uses `target`, not `achieved` or `effective`. Source publication and retrieval dates are separate. Claims use verified, disputed, unknown or unverified_source. Missing dates or evidence mean unknown, not non-adoption. Retain contributor assertions unless explicit competent evidence supports correction; record inaccessible correspondence and the precise evidence needed.

Sources referenced by adoption claims contain issuer, exact URL, source_type, language, passage, publication_date, accessed_on, access and method. Use `official_standard_body`, `official_government`, `official_law`, or `other_unverified`. Record each failed attempt; snippets may identify leads but do not verify facts or reachability. Source access is reachable, unreachable or unknown. A failed check never advances verified_on. Do not store entire copyrighted standards, private email or personal contact details.

Read the actual source, then independently compare the final claim with it. Verify country, edition, date meaning and authority. For ETSI inspect Target and Achieved columns separately; verify completed OJ citation against the relevant WAD/EAA legal record. For draft standards retain brackets, unresolved commencement and expected dates in the evidence. Meaning-sensitive public text receives an isolated no-history source-fidelity review under review.md. Store exact reviewed text, source comparison and row hashes in a version-bound report. Human maintainer review remains necessary.

## Publication and handoff

Keep the five columns, label dates by event, and include scope/qualifications in Additional information. Show last verification beside the specific supported claim; never date an entire row as verified because only its link was checked. Keep inherited unverified detail identifiable, with a concise note when necessary. Correct empty link text and inspect rendered table output. Do not turn the public page into a research log.

Assess adoption, monitoring, sanctions and enforcement for each new evidence event. Country events live in canonical deliveries; include adoption with domain `adoption` and its canonical record path. Do not retrofit every historical event. A new source supporting another domain needs an explicit research handoff, not an unsupported public addition. An absent destination can be not_applicable with a reason; record a concrete future-page handoff in adoption questions when registration is needed. EU-wide events live in the global record's deliveries, not duplicated into every country or the existing country-only routing projection.

Process changes have their own draft PR. Content may use a clearly dependent draft based on that process branch; after a maintainer merges the prerequisite, refresh and retarget to main. Do not merge either draft. Before each publication compare main, open PRs and pending branches, coordinate shared country files, and update the existing adoption draft rather than creating duplicate corrections. Follow the common research budgets: ten minutes per jurisdiction and thirty minutes per run, two attempts per failing URL and two targeted follow-up searches per unresolved question. Include actual timing and remaining budget in run notes; stop research at the limit and retain specific next actions.

## Recurring maintenance

Use the current-chat weekly scheduled task, Monday 09:00 Europe/Stockholm, with monthly and quarterly work selected within that task. No GitHub Actions change or reuse of the EAA watcher's state/lease branches is authorised. The scheduler prompt must read this file from current main; until this setup is merged, inspect the known adoption drafts and update those drafts only. Do not bypass human review to activate main.

On each run:

1. Read current main and adoption draft heads, check overlap, and resume unresolved work before opening anything new. Use one active adoption run; if another run is active, leave its work untouched. Keep a local run journal in this chat's outputs with start/end, source attempts, candidate decisions and notification history. Repository evidence belongs in reviewable draft commits, not a runtime branch. Preserve the journal across runs; if it is missing, reconstruct from records/PRs and report coverage uncertainty rather than assuming no pending work.
2. Check ETSI publication/schedule, directive-specific OJ sources and active drafts weekly. Check national catalogues and government guidance monthly; quarterly perform a full claim audit and discover missing jurisdictions as leads only. `check_adoption.py --due` lists overdue claim and domain checks. Select unattempted then oldest due entries, with unresolved high-impact issues first; persist deferred work and continue the next week. Do not label a monthly/quarterly cycle complete until every scoped row was covered. Discovering a country does not authorise adding it.
3. Compare substantive facts in source language with previous evidence. Ignore page navigation and styling. A changed hash or a first readable observation is a candidate, not an established legal change. Keep event IDs and pending candidates stable across retries. Check the same source with at most two access attempts, including at most one ordinary-browser attempt.
4. Record successful, failed and deferred checks separately. Advance last_monthly_review or last_full_review only when that row's corresponding checklist is completed, even when unchanged. Retain verified_on on failed checks. Unchanged verification can update research metadata without public edits; do not rewrite unsupported inherited claims. Use claim-specific next_review_due of seven days for active EU/NZ milestones and thirty days for settled national claims; full audit remains quarterly.
5. Verify candidates, route evidence, run isolated wording review and validators, then update a draft. Never submit forms, send correspondence, approve, merge or enable auto-merge. For supported material changes aim to prepare a draft within seven days of detection; record missed targets and reasons. Publication timing depends on human review.
6. Notify only for material supported findings, a new draft, completion of the initial baseline, or an actionable persistent blocker. Treat a failure as persistent after two separate runs, not two attempts; suppress repeat alerts while unchanged. A quiet run is not proof of comprehensive freshness.

## Checks

Run `python3 .github/scripts/check-country-records.py`, `python3 .github/scripts/check_adoption.py --require-coverage`, and `python3 .github/scripts/test_adoption.py`, plus existing content checks. The setup-only PR may run without --require-coverage before the content baseline exists. The checker validates structure, evidence references, date semantics, row mappings and review hashes; it does not certify legal interpretation, source authenticity or live reachability. Do not modify the events-calendar date checker or GitHub Actions. Record unavailable checks honestly.
